comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased 2% to $33.77 billion in 2024, aided by lower CIE commercial real estate impairments and prior year one-time charges like the GreenSky write-down, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction expenses, resulting in an efficiency ratio improvement to 63.1% from 74.6%.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose a 'timing impact' or specific year-over-year variance drivers in their Executive Overview, but they differ in the nature of the comparison. JPMorgan explicitly quantifies the impact of an acquisition (First Republic) by comparing the full twelve-month 2024 impact against an eight-month impact in 2023, labeling this a 'timing impact'. In contrast, Goldman Sachs discusses the drivers of its operating expense change, noting a 2% decrease driven by lower impairments and prior-year one-time charges (like the GreenSky write-down) compared to higher expenses in the prior year. While both address how prior-year comparisons affect current results, JPM's focus is on acquisition integration timing, whereas GS focuses on operational efficiency and non-recurring charge normalization.

sentences.text: As a result, the year-to-date results include the twelve-month impact of First Republic compared with eight months in the prior-year period.
Where meaningful to the results, this is referred to in this Form 10-K as the "timing impact" of First Republic.

Operating expenses were $33.77 billion for 2024, 2% lower than 2023, reflecting decreases driven by significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in consolidated investment entities (CIEs) and other significant expenses recognized in the prior year, including the write-down of identifiable intangible assets related to GreenSky Holdings, LLC (GreenSky), an impairment of goodwill related to Consumer platforms and the FDIC special assessment fee.
